title: It is 1 AM and the urge is loud
subtitle: 3-minute grounding and practical support

cues.text: Take a moment to notice where you are. You do not need to argue with every thought or act on every urge. Follow these prompts at a pace that feels comfortable.
Notice your body. Let your shoulders settle if that feels comfortable. Try an easy, unforced breath. If focusing on breathing is uncomfortable, simply notice your surroundings.
An urge can feel urgent without requiring an immediate response. Its intensity may change over time. You can choose to step away from the screen or reach out for support.
An unwanted thought is not the same as choosing an action. You do not need to examine or resolve every thought. Return your attention to what is in front of you.
If it is useful, notice whether you need rest, company, comfort or a change of environment. You do not have to find a perfect explanation.
Choose one small next action. You might drink some water, put your phone aside, change rooms or contact someone you trust. You may leave this practice whenever you wish.

title: Starting again after a setback
subtitle: 4-minute reflection and a practical next step

cues.text: Take a moment before deciding what to do next. A setback does not erase your earlier efforts. Choose a manageable next step rather than punishing yourself.
You can acknowledge a choice you regret without treating it as a verdict on your worth. Your earlier efforts still matter.
If it would help, consider one practical change to your surroundings or routine. You do not need to analyse every detail of what happened.
If prayer is helpful to you, bring an honest sentence to God. You can also simply sit quietly. You do not need to repeat this practice until it feels right.
You do not need to solve everything tonight. Choose one practical action and return to your day or evening. Additional support is available if you need it.
Loneliness can be difficult. You may notice how you feel without needing to judge yourself or change the feeling immediately.
Consider whether an ordinary conversation, a familiar activity or some rest would support you right now.
If prayer is helpful, offer a few quiet words to God. Breathe naturally and settle somewhere comfortable.
If you wish, think of someone safe you could contact. You do not need to explain anything private.
Choose one manageable next action. You may reach out, prepare for rest or return to your evening.
Settle somewhere comfortable. You may keep your eyes open. Take a few unhurried moments to notice how you feel, without needing to change anything.
If you wish, notice one ordinary moment from today that you appreciate. It is also fine if nothing comes to mind.
You may notice something that was difficult today, without reviewing every detail or trying to settle every concern.
Allow unfinished tasks to wait where possible. Choose any practical step that will make it easier to rest.
If you wish, offer a short closing prayer. When you are ready, put your phone aside and make room for rest.
